turns.text: A frequency threads up through the pavement before any of it reaches the ears properly — felt first, low and metallic, climbing the pads of both front paws like something underground testing whether anyone's listening. Head lifts. Whiskers angle toward the seam between two overpass supports where the vibration runs strongest.

the underpass runs low and wide beneath six lanes of elevated traffic, concrete ribbed overhead where drainage never quite dried between storms. a retinal-scanner post stands bolted to the near pylon, its beam sweeping a slow red line across the ground on a cycle timed to catch anything crossing at cat-height. the vibration comes from a transformer box wedged behind torn signage, casing dented, humming a half-tone flat. underfoot, a shard of mirrored glass lies half-buried in grit, catching the scanner's red line and throwing it sideways instead of through.

That shard gets claimed before the scanner's next pass finishes its arc — teeth close around one edge, careful of where it's sharp, and drag it back into the shadow between pylon and signage. Not the first time this exact piece has changed hands here. The weight of it settles familiar against the tongue, already knowing which corner throws the beam widest.

the shadow holds the shard's borrowed angle steady, scanner beam skating off sideways same as it did a second ago, same as it will the next hundred times. two pylons down, a scent cuts through the transformer's ozone tang — scorched fur, old and specific, the kind that doesn't wash out, laid down by something that walked through here fast and didn't stop. it's already faded past useful, more memory than trail.

That scorch-smell gets one nostril's worth of attention and no more — old business, somebody else's grudge against the district, filed next to everything else here that isn't tonight's problem. The shard stays angled at the scanner post instead. Priorities don't shift for smells with nothing left to chase.

the scanner post logs three deflections in under a minute — outside its tolerance — and flags the pylon for a physical sweep. a squat wheeled unit peels off from its dock a block up, sensor bar sweeping low, engine whining thin over wet concrete as it closes the distance faster than its usual patrol pace.

That whine gets clocked immediately, faster and closer than any patrol's usual pace, and the shard comes up on instinct — angled hard into the sensor bar's path the second it swings close enough, throwing its own light back doubled. The unit's bar stutters, overcorrects, sweeps the wrong wall entirely.

the sensor bar loses its lock mid-sweep, red line skating off across brick instead of pavement, unit rolling to a confused half-stop before its onboard logic resets and sends it trundling back toward the dock, sweep aborted, anomaly unresolved. the transformer box keeps its half-tone hum going, indifferent, same frequency as before.

Weight drops back onto the haunches once the drone's whine fades fully, shard still gripped loose in the jaw, tongue working once at a foreleg gone tense through the standoff. Small win, the kind that doesn't get remembered by anything except the muscles that just did the work.

up on the guardrail above the underpass, a shape sits hunched too still for comfort, eyes catching every color the traffic-glow throws without ever narrowing against it, blink-rate wrong for anything that sleeps regular hours. it doesn't look down. doesn't need to — attention already moved on to the next flicker before this one's finished happening.

That blink-rate reads as somebody else's malfunction, not a threat, catalogued next to broken scanners and stray hums as one more piece of the district that runs wrong without asking permission first. No claim on this stretch of guardrail. The shard gets tucked back into its gap between pylon and signage instead, home enough for tonight.

the underpass settles back into its ordinary schedule, scanner beam resuming its slow red sweep same as before the deflections started, transformer box holding its flat half-tone note, guardrail shape above gone still again except for that unblinking watch. rain finds its way down through a crack in the overhead ribbing, dripping steady onto the same six inches of concrete it's found every night this week.

Curls in against the pylon's base, shard angled where a paw can reach it without looking, ears staying tuned to the transformer's hum rather than anything sharper. The night's already logged as handled. Whatever crosses this stretch next gets read the same way everything else did — smell first, sound second, trust last.

the district keeps its low wet hum going through what's left of the dark, scanner and transformer and guardrail watcher all holding their separate patient frequencies, none of them quite in tune with each other. down at the pylon's base, the borrowed shard keeps its stolen angle steady, ready for the beam's next pass, same as it'll be ready tomorrow and the night after that.

Eyes drop to slits, the shard's cold edge a small, certain weight against one paw. Sleep comes easy enough once the scanner's rhythm stops reading like a threat and goes back to being just another sound this stretch of concrete makes every night.

the underpass holds its watch through the rest of the dark — beam sweeping, transformer humming, rain finding its same six inches of concrete — patient the way only infrastructure built to outlast its maintenance schedule ever gets to be, indifferent to the small mirrored thing that beat it twice tonight and slept anyway.
